reproduction_target: A genome-wide computational screen for 5'UTR exons that can be skipped to remove repressive upstream ORFs (uORFs) in haploinsufficient disease genes, followed by wet-lab luciferase validation of six prioritised targets. The computational reproduction target is: (1) definition of 'skippable' 5'UTR exons from MANE v1.0 (transcripts 'defined using MANE v1.0 (available at https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/refseq/MANE/MANE_human/release_1.0/)'); (2) collation of upstream start codons - 'We collated ORF calls from nine published ribo-seq studies (Supplementary Table 5)', with liftover to GRCh38 and start-codon sequence verification against hg38; (3) identification of 953 autosomal-dominant haploinsufficient genes from ClinVar, GenCC, Gene2Phenotype, ClinGen dosage sensitivity and Genomics England/PanelApp; (4) prevalence estimation from Genomics England 100kGP v18 (exit questionnaire + diagnostic discovery table via the RLabkey API) plus ClinVar and Kaplanis et al. Supplementary Table 1; (5) UK Biobank splice-disrupting variant counts (application 81050); (6) automated prioritisation producing 79 candidate exons; (7) 5'UTR feature annotation with RNAfold, QGRS Mapper, RBP-Tar, IRESbase and miRStart 2.0; (8) long-read (ONT, SQANTI3 + CPAT) and short-read (BrainVar, DEXSeq-derived exon annotation) human cortex RNA-seq analyses of target-exon inclusion; and (9) the statistics reported for those analyses (Fisher's exact test, LOESS fit, ANOVA + Tukey). The wet-lab arm (psiCHECK2 cloning, HeLa transfection, dual-luciferase assay, RNA extraction, RT-qPCR) is scored OOS. Two author code repositories are named in the Data and code availability statement: https://github.com/Computational-Rare-Disease-Genomics-WHG/skip_uORFs/ (Snakemake, covers the screen) and https://github.com/Computational-Rare-Disease-Genomics-WHG/RNA_structure (Snakemake, covers RNAfold). No repository is named for the RNA-seq analyses or for the statistics.
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool/analysis, built from the Methods section of the v1 JATS full text plus the two named repository landing pages and their READMEs (prose only; no workflow source was read - that is Stage 2). The four hosted 5'UTR feature-annotation services (QGRS Mapper, RBP-Tar, IRESbase, miRStart 2.0) are kept as four separate steps because they are four distinct named tool invocations under the rubric's one-step-per-named-tool rule, even though all four score identically; a reader who prefers a merged 'hosted feature annotation' step would obtain S = 13 with the same verdict distribution shape. The manual final selection of the six experimental targets is recorded as C7 with layer W and verdict OOS - the README states verbatim 'This automated approach was used as a first indiciation, the genes selected for experimental work were the outcome of further discussion and manual assessment', i.e. it is human-judgement curation with no machine-executable target, so it is excluded from S (S = 16, not 17). The LOESS fit (C15) is separated from the exon-level quantification (C14) because it is a distinct modelling operation on the quantified output. Wet-lab bench steps W1-W5 are OOS. S = 16, W = 6 (C7 + W1-W5).

steps.label: Identification of 5'UTR exons that can be skipped: 'Transcripts were defined using MANE v1.0 (available at https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/refseq/MANE/MANE_human/release_1.0/). Skippable exons were defined as any exon that is flanked by introns in the 5'UTR. This excludes the first 5'UTR exon, and typically the final exon of the 5'UTR, unless there is an intron between the end of the 5'UTR and the start of the CDS.' Implemented in the skip_uORFs Snakemake rule `exon_targets` (README: 'This rule combines MANE annotations, with the collation of uORFs, and haploinsufficient genes, to identifiy 5'UTR exons which are flanked by other 5'UTR exons')

Collation of upstream start codons from ribo-seq: 'We collated ORF calls from nine published ribo-seq studies (Supplementary Table 5). Where necessary, we used liftover to transform genome coordinates to GRCh38 and adjusted coordinates such that canonical ORFs aligned with their annotations in UCSC genome browser (1-based). The sequence of the start codon was retrieved against the hg38 reference. Where sources reported the sequence of the start codon, ORFs with a start codon sequence mismatch were excluded.' Implemented in the skip_uORFs rule `uORFs`. The nine source datasets are identified only in Supplementary Table 5 (not fetched at stage 1); no liftover tool name, version or chain file is stated

Identification of 953 autosomal-dominant haploinsufficient genes: 'We used ClinVar, GenCC, Gene2Phenotype (G2P), ClinGen gene-disease validity, and Genomics England to identify 953 genes associated with dominant loss-of-function haploinsufficient disorders', with four explicit inclusion rules (G2P 'Definitive'/'Strong' + 'monoallelic' + 'absent gene product' across six panels; ClinGen dosage-sensitivity haploinsufficiency score 3; PanelApp 'Green' + 'MONOALLELIC'; GenCC 'Definitive'/'Strong' + dominant inheritance; plus a >=8 pathogenic/likely-pathogenic pLoF ClinVar filter where variant mechanism was unavailable). Implemented in the skip_uORFs rule `haploinsufficient_genes`. No download date, release tag or snapshot identifier is given for any of ClinVar, GenCC, G2P, ClinGen or PanelApp - all five are continuously updated resources

Prevalence estimation: 'We used 100kGP v18, and loss-of-function variant counts from ClinVar (see above), and in Supplementary Table 1 from Kaplanis et al to estimate prevalence. For 100kGP, diagnostic data was obtained from the Genomics England exit questionnaire (12,024 unique variants in 9,841 individuals) and diagnostic discovery table (2,394 unique variants in 2,452 individuals respectively) via the RLabkey API. Where required, variants were remapped to GRCh38 using the UCSC LiftOver tool.' Filtering to pathogenic/likely pathogenic/diagnostic-discovery and single-gene mapping is reported with intermediate counts (8,145 -> 5,752 unique variants in 6,056 individuals). Controlled access with a documented DAC path: 'Research on the de-identified patient data used in this publication can be carried out in the Genomics England Research Environment subject to a collaborative agreement... interested readers may contact research-network@genomicsengland.co.uk'; project ID 354 named in Acknowledgements. The analysis runs inside the Genomics England Research Environment; the repository is not stated to contain the in-enclave code

UK Biobank splice-disrupting variant counting at target-exon splice sites: 'We also included exon targets with at least one probable splice-disrupting variant in UK Biobank (n=44), hypothesising that this indicates that skipping the target exon is tolerated. Data were accessed under UK Biobank application number 81050.' The prioritised-targets output carries the column 'UKBB_variants_at_exon_splice_sites: the number of variants found in UKBB impacting splice acceptor or donor sites of the target exon' (skip_uORFs README). No UK Biobank data release/field ID, no variant-annotation tool, and no operational definition of 'probable splice-disrupting' are given

Automated prioritisation of gene/exon targets (skip_uORFs rule `prioritisation`): 'This prioritises exon targets based on: the predicted consequence of exon skipping on the 5'UTR and canonical translation, strength of association with haploinsufficient human disease and organ specificity to a closed system (CNS or EYE), estimated patient numbers.' Methods give the explicit criteria: removal of sixteen targets predicted to cause uORF extensions; retention only where a high-confidence uORF initiates within the exon (n = 52); prioritisation of exons whose skipping removes a uORF within 50 bp of, or overlapping, the CDS, or >3 high-confidence uORF start codons; cross-referencing GenCC associations against MONDO hierarchies 0021147, 0700092 and 0005503; top-60% thresholding on ClinVar/Kaplanis/100kGP counts

Manual final selection of the six exon targets taken forward to functional validation: 'Six exon targets were selected for functional validation based on their strength of association with developmental disorder, estimated prevalence, and predicted consequence of exon skipping on translation... In addition, TSC1 was selected due to its unique 5'UTR structure for interrogating the impact of multiple uORF perturbations.' The skip_uORFs README states verbatim: 'This automated approach was used as a first indiciation, the genes selected for experimental work were the outcome of further discussion and manual assessment.' Human-judgement curation with no machine-executable target

RNA secondary-structure / stem-loop prediction: 'Stem loops were identified using RNAfold. A 60ntd sliding window was applied to the 5'UTR of each gene, plus the first 50ntds of the CDS, as determined using 5'UTR annotations from MANE and human reference genome hg38 (available at http://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenpath/hg38/bigZips/latest). Stem loops which were located wholly within another stem loop were excluded.' Code repository named: https://github.com/Computational-Rare-Disease-Genomics-WHG/RNA_structure (snakefile + config.yaml + environment.yml + scripts/). The tool is cited as 'ViennaRNA Package 2.0' (a paper citation, not a build version), no RNAfold command-line options (temperature, dangling-end model, energy parameter set) are given, and the hg38 reference is fetched from a literal '.../bigZips/latest' path

G-quadruplex identification: 'G-quadruplexes were identified with QGRS mapper.' Hosted third-party web server, cited by reference only (Kikin, D'Antonio & Bagga, 'QGRS Mapper: a web-based server for predicting G-quadruplexes in nucleotide sequences'). No URL printed in Methods, no server version, no access date, and none of the QGRS parameters (max QGRS length, minimum G-group size, loop-length range, G-score threshold) are reported. No wrapper code deposited

RNA-binding-protein site identification: 'RBPs were identified with RBP-Tar available at https://rbp-tar.biodata.ceitec.cz/.' Hosted third-party web server. No version, no access date, no score/threshold or RBP set reported; no wrapper code or result export deposited

IRES search: 'IRES were searched with IRES base.' Hosted third-party database, cited by reference only; no URL in Methods, no database version or release date, no search parameters or match criteria reported, no code

microRNA binding-site analysis: 'The binding of microRNA to the 5'UTR was investigated with miRStart 2.0, but no miRNA binding sites were observed.' Hosted third-party web server, version given only as the product name '2.0'; no access date, no query parameters, no thresholds, no code. This is a reported negative result whose derivation cannot be re-checked

Long-read cortex RNA-seq analysis: 'Oxford Nanopore Technologies long read RNA sequence data was generated from 26 prenatal and 21 postnatal frontal cortex samples are described in Bamford et al. 2024. The transcripts were annotated using SQANTI3 and CPAT was used to predict the open reading frame and coding potential of the transcripts. Transcript isoforms were considered protein-coding if the CPAT coding probability was the recommended >0.364, the open reading frame had a canonical stop site, 80% of the CDS as defined by MANE was included, and the start of the transcript was within 500bp of a CAGE peak. From these reads, we calculated the proportion in which the target exon was flanked by the first and third 5'UTR exon and deemed skippable.' No accession is given in this paper (the data are attributed to a 2024 bioRxiv preprint, 10.1101/2024.05.24.595768); no SQANTI3 or CPAT version; no CAGE atlas version; no code repository is named for this analysis

Short-read cortex RNA-seq exon-level quantification: 'Short read RNA sequence data from 116 prenatal and 60 postnatal dorsolateral prefrontal cortex samples are described in Werling et al. Exon-level expression was quantified from bulk RNA-seq data using exon annotations derived from DEXSeq. For each sample, read fragments overlapping the 5' UTR target exon region, and a length-matched portion at the 5' end of the CDS, were counted and median of those fragments were calculated. Expression values were normalized to counts per million (CPM) to account for differences in sequencing depth.' BrainVar is referenced by publication only - no dbGaP/SRA/Synapse accession is printed in this paper; no aligner is named at all; no DEXSeq version; no code repository named for this analysis

Developmental expression-trend modelling: 'An estimated scatterplot smoothing (LOESS) curve was fitted to the data to capture expression trends over time, with shaded areas indicating the 95% confidence interval of the fit.' No software named, no version, and no LOESS parameters (span, degree, family, weighting) or confidence-interval method reported; no code deposited

Test of developmental change in target-exon skippability for CTCF: 'inclusion of the target exon was significantly higher in prenatal compared to postnatal samples (91.3% vs 54.1%, Fisher's exact test, odds ratio = 0.11, p = 5.31x10-8, Figure 2B, Supplementary Figure 2)'. The test is named and the statistics are reported, but the contingency table construction (read-level vs transcript-level counting unit), sidedness, and multiple-testing handling across the tested genes are not stated; no code and no software version

Statistical analysis of the dual-luciferase and RT-qPCR readouts: 'Samples were analysed with the Promega GloMax Turner 20/20n Luminometer and the data analysed using R. Statistical significance was assessed using ANOVA and Tukey multiple comparison tests.' and 'Relative mRNA expression was calculated using the 2^(-DDCt) method.' R is cited with no version; no model specification (factors, blocking by replicate/plate, transformation), no per-well raw luminescence or Cq values deposited, and no analysis script

5'UTR reporter construct generation: 'The 5' UTR sequences (Supplementary Table 3), extending up to the primary ATG initiation codon and including two additional nucleotides (cg) at their 3' side to maintain the reading frame, were custom synthesized by Azenta Biosciences, Germany. These UTRs were then excised and ligated into the NheI site located upstream of the Renilla luciferase gene in the dual-luciferase vector psiCHECK2 (Promega).'

HeLa cell culture and transfection: 'HeLa cells were cultured in DMEM with 10% FBS in 6 well plates seeded at 140,000 cells/ml and incubated at 37oC... cells were transfected with 500ng of the luciferase reporter constructs using the Qiagen Effectene kit, following the manufacturer's instructions.'

Dual-luciferase reporter assay: 'Twenty four hours post-transfection, cells were washed with 1X PBS and lysed with 1X Passive Lysis Buffer (Promega). Renilla and Firefly luciferase activities were measured using the Dual-Glo Luciferase Assay System (Promega)... Renilla luciferase activity was normalised to Firefly luciferase activity.'

RNA extraction and reverse transcription: 'RNA extractions from cells were performed using TRI reagent (invitrogen) as per the manufacturer's phase-separation protocol. One microgram of total RNA was reverse transcribed using oligo dT and M-MLV reverse transcriptase (Invitrogen), according to manufacturer's instructions. No-RT controls were included in parallel.'

RT-qPCR: 'qPCR was performed using the BioRad CFX Connect Real-Time System. cDNA was diluted at a 1:10 ratio, and 5 ul of the diluted cDNA were used in a total reaction volume of 14 ul... Primers used for RT-qPCR are listed in Supplementary Table 4.'

headline.static_readiness: 0/16 (0%) - stage1 ceiling only, no R-star (R-star needs stage-2 code verification)
headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: 7/16 (44%) of computational steps reach RI at stage 1; the remaining 9 are NI, none are X. The paper splits sharply into two halves, and the split is exactly along the boundary of the two deposited repositories. The screen half (C1-C6, C8) reaches RI in full: two public Snakemake repositories are named in the Data and code availability statement, both resolve 200, and skip_uORFs ships environment.yml + environment_full.yml ('provides all packages, dependancies, versions and builds') + a 292 KB renv.lock, so the version axis is claim-capped at 1 only because Stage 1 refuses to credit an unexecuted lock. Two of those seven clear RI only marginally, on data rather than code grounds: C2 (the nine ribo-seq ORF-call sources are identified only in Supplementary Table 5, not fetched at stage 1) and C3 (ClinVar, GenCC, G2P, ClinGen and PanelApp are all rolling resources cited with no download date or release tag, so the 953-gene list cannot be re-derived to the same snapshot). The annotation/RNA-seq half (C9-C17) has no code at all and is uniformly NI: four hosted web services (QGRS Mapper, RBP-Tar, IRESbase, miRStart 2.0) are invoked with no version, no access date and no parameters, and neither the long-read (SQANTI3 + CPAT) nor the short-read (DEXSeq) cortex analysis, nor the LOESS/Fisher/ANOVA statistics, has a named repository. This IS a stage-2 candidate: capture_claim = env_lock_claimed, and the Stage-2 code check would determine whether environment_full.yml + renv.lock actually deliver environment closure and whether the workflows fetch MANE/hg38 by pinned version (class A) or from the mutable '.../hg38/bigZips/latest' path named in Methods (class C).
headline.coverage: 22 steps built from the Methods section of the v1 JATS XML (fetched 200 OK, title verified verbatim as 'Modulating splicing in 5' untranslated regions to treat rare haploinsufficient disease') plus the Data and code availability statement and the landing pages + READMEs of the two named GitHub repositories. 16 are computational C-steps counted in S; 6 are OOS (C7 manual target selection, W1-W5 bench work), giving computational coverage 16/22 = 73%. Supplementary Tables 1-5 (ribo-seq sources, 5'UTR sequences, qPCR primers) were not fetched at stage 1. No workflow source was read: Snakefiles, rules/, scripts/, environment_full.yml and renv.lock were observed only as repository-root entries, never opened.

gaps.where: C13 (long-read SQANTI3 + CPAT), C14 (short-read DEXSeq exon quantification), C15 (LOESS), C16 (Fisher's exact test), C17 (ANOVA + Tukey, 2^-DDCt)
gaps.missing: The Data and code availability statement names exactly two repositories, and both cover only the screen: 'A snakemake workflow for uORF start codon collation, haploinsufficient gene identification, target identification and prioritisation is available here: https://github.com/Computational-Rare-Disease-Genomics-WHG/skip_uORFs/' and 'RNA structure was predicted using RNAfold. Code available here: https://github.com/Computational-Rare-Disease-Genomics-WHG/RNA_structure'. Nothing is deposited for the two cortex RNA-seq analyses (which produce Figure 2 and Supplementary Figure 2) or for any of the statistics reported in Results, including the CTCF Fisher's exact test whose exact p-value (5.31x10-8) is quoted in the abstract-adjacent narrative, and the ANOVA/Tukey analysis underpinning the headline 1.4-5.5 fold translation increases.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the RNA-seq analysis code (SQANTI3/CPAT invocation, DEXSeq exon-flattening and counting, CPM normalisation) and the R scripts that produce the LOESS curves, the Fisher's exact test and the ANOVA + Tukey luciferase analysis, and cite them alongside the two existing repositories in the Data and code availability statement.

gaps.where: C2 (liftover), C8 (RNAfold), C9-C12 (QGRS Mapper, RBP-Tar, IRESbase, miRStart 2.0), C13 (SQANTI3, CPAT), C14 (DEXSeq), C15/C16/C17 (R)
gaps.missing: Version recording in Methods prose is close to absent (gap 2a). RNAfold is cited only as 'ViennaRNA Package 2.0', which is the title of the 2011 Algorithms Mol Biol paper rather than a build version. SQANTI3, CPAT, DEXSeq, the liftover implementation, and R itself ('the data analysed using R') carry no version at all. The four hosted services carry neither a version nor an access date, so their behaviour at the time of use is unrecoverable. The only version-like pins in prose are data versions, not software versions: MANE v1.0 and 100kGP v18. The repository-side claim (skip_uORFs README: 'environment_full.yml provides all packages, dependancies, versions and builds' plus renv.lock; RNA_structure environment.yml) is a claim only at stage 1 and covers only the two screen workflows, not the RNA-seq or statistics steps, which have no environment artifact at all.
gaps.how_to_close: State exact versions in Methods for every named tool (RNAfold/ViennaRNA build, SQANTI3, CPAT, DEXSeq, liftover, R and each R package), record the access date and full query parameters for each hosted service, and extend the environment capture to cover the RNA-seq and statistical analyses.

gaps.where: C1/C8 (MANE, hg38), C3 (ClinVar, GenCC, G2P, ClinGen dosage sensitivity, PanelApp), C13 (CAGE peak atlas, MANE)
gaps.missing: Reference-resource pinning is inconsistent. MANE is pinned well - 'MANE v1.0 (available at https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/refseq/MANE/MANE_human/release_1.0/)', a versioned directory that resolves 200. But the hg38 reference for the RNA-structure step is cited as 'http://hgdownload.soe.ucsc.edu/goldenpath/hg38/bigZips/latest', a literal 'latest' path whose contents change; and the five gene-disease resources behind the 953-gene haploinsufficient list (ClinVar, GenCC, G2P, ClinGen, PanelApp) are all continuously revised with no download date, release tag or archived snapshot recorded. A re-run today will not reproduce the 953-gene set or the 79-target list. Whether the workflows fetch these by pinned version (class A) or from mutable paths (class C) cannot be determined from prose - that is the Stage-2 check.
gaps.how_to_close: Record the download date and release identifier for every gene-disease resource (ClinVar VCF release, GenCC/PanelApp/ClinGen export dates), replace the 'bigZips/latest' hg38 reference with a fixed-version path or checksum, and deposit the frozen input snapshots (or their checksums) alongside the workflow so the screen can be replayed from a fixed state.

gaps.missing: Four of the sixteen computational steps are hosted third-party web services with no local, installable equivalent named and no deposited result export. Their availability, version and default parameters are outside the authors' control and outside any environment capture; miRStart 2.0 in particular supports a reported negative finding ('no miRNA binding sites were observed') that cannot be re-derived. RBP-Tar's URL (https://rbp-tar.biodata.ceitec.cz/) resolves 200 today, but the other three are cited by reference only with no URL printed in Methods.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the exact query inputs and the raw result exports from each service (with query date and all non-default settings), and where a downloadable/installable equivalent exists, run and pin that instead of the hosted endpoint.

gaps.where: C13 (ONT long-read cortex data), C14 (BrainVar short-read cortex data), C17 (luciferase and RT-qPCR readouts)
gaps.missing: No sequencing accession appears anywhere in this paper. The long-read data are described only as 'generated from 26 prenatal and 21 postnatal frontal cortex samples are described in Bamford et al. 2024' (a bioRxiv preprint, 10.1101/2024.05.24.595768) and the short-read data only as '116 prenatal and 60 postnatal dorsolateral prefrontal cortex samples are described in Werling et al'. A reproducer must chase two upstream publications to find any identifier, and no per-sample manifest (sample IDs, prenatal/postnatal assignment, developmental stage covariate used for the LOESS fit) is provided. Separately, the per-well luciferase and RT-qPCR measurements underlying the reported 1.4-5.5 fold effects are not deposited in any machine-readable form.
gaps.how_to_close: Print the dbGaP/SRA/Synapse/ENA accessions for both cortex cohorts directly in the Data availability statement, supply a per-sample manifest with the exact subset and covariates used, and deposit the raw luminometer and Cq measurements as a supplementary machine-readable table.

gaps.where: C2 (nine ribo-seq ORF-call source datasets, Supplementary Table 5)
gaps.missing: The uORF collation - the load-bearing input to the whole screen - is built from 'ORF calls from nine published ribo-seq studies (Supplementary Table 5)'. The identities, versions and download locations of those nine call sets exist only in a supplementary table that is not itself deposited in a repository with a DOI, and the harmonised collated ORF table is not deposited as a standalone dataset (only its column schema is documented in the skip_uORFs README).
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the nine source ORF-call files (or their DOIs/URLs with retrieval dates) and the harmonised collated uORF table as a versioned, DOI-bearing dataset, and move the source list from the supplement into a machine-readable manifest inside the repository.

gaps.where: C7 (manual six-target selection), W1-W5 (construct synthesis and cloning, HeLa culture and transfection, dual-luciferase assay, RNA extraction and RT, RT-qPCR)
gaps.missing: Six of the twenty-two steps are non-computational and are excluded from S. The bench protocols are described at conventional Methods density (cell density, DNA amounts, timings, kits and instruments are all named), so this is a scope exclusion rather than a documentation failure. C7 is scored OOS on a different ground: the README states the final six genes 'were the outcome of further discussion and manual assessment', so the step from the automated ranking to the experimental panel is human judgement with no machine-executable target and no recorded decision trail.
gaps.how_to_close: For C7, record the deliberation that turned the automated ranking into the six-gene panel (which candidates were dropped and why) as a versioned decision log in the repository, so the selection is at least auditable even though it is not executable.

gaps.missing: Neither repository has a release, a tag, or a license. The GitHub API returns an empty releases array and an empty tags array for skip_uORFs, and 'license': null for both. The paper cites bare default-branch URLs, so the cited code is a moving target: skip_uORFs README opens with the line 'Review branch', suggesting the state a reader sees may not be the state used for the manuscript. Without a license, third-party re-use rights are formally undefined even though the code is publicly readable.
gaps.how_to_close: Cut a tagged release for each repository at the manuscript state, archive both to Zenodo for a versioned DOI, cite the DOI rather than the bare branch URL in the Data and code availability statement, and add an explicit open-source license.
